[bold #D75FFF]◆ EPIC sase-ku[/bold #D75FFF]
[dim]  Title: [bold #D7AFFF][/dim]sase monitor hardening — a supervisor that cannot silently orphan, [/bold #D7AFFF]
[dim]         [bold #D7AFFF][/dim]wedge, or lie[/bold #D7AFFF]
[dim]   Goal: [#D7D7AF][/dim]The monitor supervisor survives every command shape a real build [/#D7D7AF]
[dim]         [#D7D7AF][/dim]throws at it — continuous output, partial lines, binary bytes, [/#D7D7AF]
[dim]         [#D7D7AF][/dim]backgrounded grandchildren, TERM-ignoring children — enforces its [/#D7D7AF]
[dim]         [#D7D7AF][/dim]deadline on every tick, never leaves a live process group behind [/#D7D7AF]
[dim]         [#D7D7AF][/dim]when it dies, reconciles wedged lanes without a human, and only [/#D7D7AF]
[dim]         [#D7D7AF][/dim]reports a monitor terminal once the claim, the log, and the [/#D7D7AF]
[dim]         [#D7D7AF][/dim]follow-up have actually been settled.[/#D7D7AF]
[dim] Counts: [bold #D7AFFF][/dim]10[dim][/bold #D7AFFF] phases[dim][/dim] · [bold #D7AFFF][/dim]6[dim][/bold #D7AFFF] waves[/dim]
[dim]   Path: [#87AFFF][/dim]plans:202608/[bold #87AFFF][/#87AFFF]monitor_hardening.md[/bold #87AFFF]
[dim] Prompt: [#87AFFF][/dim]prompts/202608/monitor_hardening.md[/#87AFFF]
[dim]   Bead: [#87AFFF][/dim]sase-ku[/#87AFFF]
[dim]   Page: [#87AFFF][/dim]https://github.com/sase-org/sase--beads/blob/main/pages/sase-ku/[bold #87AFFF][/#87AFFF]README.md[/bold #87AFFF]
[dim]  1 [bold #AF87FF][/dim]◆ [bold #D7AFFF][/bold #AF87FF]Monitor supervision fields on the agent scan wire[/bold #D7AFFF]             [bold black on #87D7FF] small  [/bold black on #87D7FF]
    [#AF87FF]wire[dim] · [dim][/dim]no dependencies[/#AF87FF][/dim]
    [#D7D7AF]wire: add the process-identity, settlement, idle-timeout, and [/#D7D7AF]
    [#D7D7AF]follow-up-output marker fields to the Rust `AgentMetaWire` and its [/#D7D7AF]
    [#D7D7AF]Python mirrors so the hardening phases have somewhere durable to record [/#D7D7AF]
    [#D7D7AF]them.[/#D7D7AF]
    [#D7D7AF][/#D7D7AF]
[dim]  2 [bold #AF87FF][/dim]◆ [bold #D7AFFF][/bold #AF87FF]Rebuild the supervisor's stream and wait loop[/bold #D7AFFF]                 [bold black on #FFD75F] medium [/bold black on #FFD75F]
    [#AF87FF]stream[dim] · [dim][/dim]no dependencies[/#AF87FF][/dim]
    [#D7D7AF]stream: replace the blocking line-oriented `readline()` loop with a [/#D7D7AF]
    [#D7D7AF]pipe-backed bounded writer plus a `child.poll()` tick loop, guard the [/#D7D7AF]
    [#D7D7AF]whole supervisor lifecycle in `try`/`finally`, make every reader [/#D7D7AF]
    [#D7D7AF]rotation-aware, and pass the monitor workflow to `release_workspace()`.[/#D7D7AF]
    [#D7D7AF][/#D7D7AF]
[dim]  3 [bold #AF87FF][/dim]◆ [bold #D7AFFF][/bold #AF87FF]Durable process identity for the supervisor and its child[/bold #D7AFFF]     [bold black on #87D7FF] small  [/bold black on #87D7FF]
    [#AF87FF]identity[dim] · [dim][/dim]after wire, stream[/#AF87FF][/dim]
    [#D7D7AF]identity: persist the monitored command's pgid and a boot-id/start-ticks[/#D7D7AF]
    [#D7D7AF]identity for the supervisor pid before the command can outlive its [/#D7D7AF]
    [#D7D7AF]recorder, scrub agent identity from the command's environment, and [/#D7D7AF]
    [#D7D7AF]validate identity before signalling.[/#D7D7AF]
    [#D7D7AF][/#D7D7AF]
[dim]  4 [bold #AF87FF][/dim]◆ [bold #D7AFFF][/bold #AF87FF]Transactional monitor start and settlement[/bold #D7AFFF]                    [bold black on #FFD75F] medium [/bold black on #FFD75F]
    [#AF87FF]transaction[dim] · [dim][/dim]after identity[/#AF87FF][/dim]
    [#D7D7AF]transaction: take a per-lane lock inside `start_monitor()`, hold the [/#D7D7AF]
    [#D7D7AF]command behind a go barrier until the workspace claim is secured, [/#D7D7AF]
    [#D7D7AF]fingerprint the request for honest idempotency, and write the terminal [/#D7D7AF]
    [#D7D7AF]marker only after settlement.[/#D7D7AF]
    [#D7D7AF][/#D7D7AF]
[dim]  5 [bold #AF87FF][/dim]◆ [bold #D7AFFF][/bold #AF87FF]Active, complete reconciliation of dead supervisors[/bold #D7AFFF]           [bold black on #FFD75F] medium [/bold black on #FFD75F]
    [#AF87FF]reconcile[dim] · [dim][/dim]after transaction[/#AF87FF][/dim]
    [#D7D7AF]reconcile: make dead-supervisor reconciliation kill the surviving tree, [/#D7D7AF]
    [#D7D7AF]release the claim, and dispose of the dropped follow-up; run it from [/#D7D7AF]
    [#D7D7AF]`list`, the TUI, and the axe scheduler rather than only from `stop`; [/#D7D7AF]
    [#D7D7AF]mark pre-reboot monitors `lost`.[/#D7D7AF]
    [#D7D7AF][/#D7D7AF]
[dim]  6 [bold #AF87FF][/dim]◆ [bold #D7AFFF][/bold #AF87FF]--idle-timeout for commands that hang without exiting[/bold #D7AFFF]         [bold black on #87D7FF] small  [/bold black on #87D7FF]
    [#AF87FF]idle[dim] · [dim][/dim]after wire, stream[/#AF87FF][/dim]
    [#D7D7AF]idle: add an opt-in idle timeout that fires when a monitored command has[/#D7D7AF]
    [#D7D7AF]produced no output for N seconds, so `--timeout` can be generous without[/#D7D7AF]
    [#D7D7AF]being useless.[/#D7D7AF]
    [#D7D7AF][/#D7D7AF]
[dim]  7 [bold #AF87FF][/dim]◆ [bold #D7AFFF][/bold #AF87FF]Follow-up prompt trust boundary and inherited routing[/bold #D7AFFF]         [bold black on #FFD75F] medium [/bold black on #FFD75F]
    [#AF87FF]followup[dim] · [dim][/dim]after wire, stream[/#AF87FF][/dim]
    [#D7D7AF]followup: treat retained command output as untrusted data in the [/#D7D7AF]
    [#D7D7AF]composed prompt, add `--next-output none|tail|file`, fence the command [/#D7D7AF]
    [#D7D7AF]and cwd cells, and carry the starter's model and reasoning effort to the[/#D7D7AF]
    [#D7D7AF]follow-up agent.[/#D7D7AF]
    [#D7D7AF][/#D7D7AF]
[dim]  8 [bold #AF87FF][/dim]◆ [bold #D7AFFF][/bold #AF87FF]Close the monitor fidelity gaps[/bold #D7AFFF]                               [bold black on #87D7FF] small  [/bold black on #87D7FF]
    [#AF87FF]fidelity[dim] · [dim][/dim]after transaction[/#AF87FF][/dim]
    [#D7D7AF]fidelity: print the start summary before the handoff kill, write [/#D7D7AF]
    [#D7D7AF]`monitor_output_path` and `run_started_at`, and read the member's own [/#D7D7AF]
    [#D7D7AF]marker files instead of re-querying the artifact index in every polling [/#D7D7AF]
    [#D7D7AF]loop.[/#D7D7AF]
    [#D7D7AF][/#D7D7AF]
[dim]  9 [bold #AF87FF][/dim]◆ [bold #D7AFFF][/bold #AF87FF]Monitor documentation and skill hazards[/bold #D7AFFF]                       [bold black on #87D7FF] small  [/bold black on #87D7FF]
    [#AF87FF]docs[dim] · [dim][/dim]after reconcile, idle, followup, fidelity[/#AF87FF][/dim]
    [#D7D7AF]docs: document the new supervision guarantees, states, and flags in [/#D7D7AF]
    [#D7D7AF]`docs/monitors.md`, and tighten the `/sase_monitor` skill with the [/#D7D7AF]
    [#D7D7AF]hazard list and the flags it never mentioned.[/#D7D7AF]
    [#D7D7AF][/#D7D7AF]
[dim]  10 [bold #AF87FF][/dim]◆ [bold #D7AFFF][/bold #AF87FF]End-to-end hardening exercises[/bold #D7AFFF]                               [bold black on #5FD7AF] xsmall [/bold black on #5FD7AF]
    [#AF87FF]exercises[dim] · [dim][/dim]after docs[/#AF87FF][/dim]
    [#D7D7AF]exercises: run real monitors and agents against the regression matrix [/#D7D7AF]
    [#D7D7AF]rows that automated tests cannot express, and report what the CLI, TUI, [/#D7D7AF]
    [#D7D7AF]and follow-up agent actually did.[/#D7D7AF]
